concepts.title: Five Year Plans and the Goals of Planning
concepts.definition: After independence India adopted planning through Five Year Plans drafted by the Planning Commission, with goals of growth, modernisation, self-reliance and equity, and the first plan focused on agriculture while the second launched Mahalanobis heavy industry strategy.
concepts.key_idea: Planning set sectoral targets through plans, and the public sector was given the command over core and heavy industries under the Industrial Policy Resolution of 1956.
question_patterns: define planning and the role of the planning commission
state the goals of five year plans in india
compare the first and second five year plans
what was the mahalanobis strategy of industrialisation
what did the industrial policy resolution of 1956 provide
why was self reliance a planning goal

solution_steps.explain: Note the period and focus of the plan in question.
Link the plan to growth, modernisation, self-reliance or equity.
State the sectoral emphasis and its rationale.

concepts.title: Agriculture: Land Reforms, Green Revolution and Marketing
concepts.definition: Agricultural policy combined institutional reforms of land ceiling and consolidation with the Green Revolution package of high yielding variety seeds, fertilisers and assured irrigation from the mid 1960s, plus regulated markets and minimum support price to stabilise farmer incomes.
concepts.key_idea: The Green Revolution raised foodgrain output and made India self-sufficient in food, but benefited mainly well irrigated regions and larger farmers.
question_patterns: what was the green revolution and its components
explain land reforms undertaken after independence
what is the role of minimum support price for farmers
how do regulated markets help farmers
state the effects and limitations of the green revolution
why was food security a concern of agricultural policy

solution_steps.explain: Place land reform against the HYV package.
Note output growth, self sufficiency and regional imbalance.
Recall MSP and regulated market roles.

concepts.title: Industry: Industrial Licensing and Public Private Split
concepts.definition: Industrial policy reserved core industries for the public sector, controlled private entry through industrial licensing, and channelled small scale reservation for employment, which built a broad industrial base but created inefficiency, shortage and licensing raj by the 1980s.
concepts.key_idea: Industrial licensing constrained private investment decisions, and small scale industry reservation aimed to protect employment intensive units.
question_patterns: what is industrial licensing and why was it used
state the role of the public sector in indian industrialisation
why were some products reserved for small scale industry
what is meant by licensing raj
evaluate the industrial policy of 1956
how did industrial controls affect growth up to 1990

solution_steps.explain: Recall licensing, reservation and public sector roles.
Link each control to self reliance or employment aims.
Weigh base building against inefficiency and shortages.

concepts.title: Trade Policy: Inward Looking Import Substitution
concepts.definition: Trade policy till 1990 was inward looking, using tariffs and quotas to protect domestic industry under import substitution, which conserved foreign exchange and nurtured industry but raised costs, reduced competition and limited export growth.
concepts.key_idea: Tariffs are taxes on imports and quotas fix physical limits, both shielding domestic producers from foreign competition.
question_patterns: define import substitution and its objectives
how do tariffs and quotas protect domestic industry
what were the effects of inward looking trade policy
why did export growth remain low till 1990
distinguish tariff and quota as trade barriers
state the critique of import substituting industrialisation

solution_steps.explain: Note whether protection came from tariff or quota.
Link the barrier to import substitution.
List gains of industry building against cost and competition losses.
